title: Sponsor Bridge Update Playbook and Qtr Summary
content:
PURPOSE
This is a lightweight, repeatable playbook for sponsor-facing bridge updates and the customer-facing quarterly recap email. Goal: give CS teams a concise structure to align exec sponsors, surface risks early, celebrate high-impact wins, and drive toward renewal asks or capacity decisions.

INTENDED AUDIENCE
- Primary: CSM assigned to the account + Solutions Eng lead
- Secondary: AE, Renewal Rep, Product exec (if relevant)

WHEN TO USE
- Quarterly sponsor touch (QBR cadence)
- Mid-quarter ‘bridge’ update when risk or runway changes
- Before any renewal negotiation to prime the sponsor

OWNER / CADENCE
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel, CSM Lead
- Cadence: standard QBR (quarterly) and ad-hoc bridge updates as needed

SUCCESS METRICS (use to prep the slide deck/email)
- NPS / satisfaction trend since last QBR: +/− points
- Consumption vs committed capacity: % of commit used, burn rate trend
- Latency & error rate deltas for production routes used by customer
- Cost per 1k tokens (moving average) and any optimization wins
- Renewal likelihood: Green/Amber/Red (simple 3-pt) with rationale

8-POINT SPONSOR BRIDGE CHECKLIST (quick for meeting prep)
1) Executive one-liner: Current overall health and ask (<= 30 words).
2) Top 2 wins since last meeting (impact + metric).
3) One customer pain/risk with context and mitigation plan.
4) Consumption snapshot vs commit and forecast (next 90 days).
5) Ops health: latency P95, error spikes, incident summary (last 90d).
6) Roadmap alignment: any upcoming Redwood features that affect customer.
7) Renewal/contract ask (timing, numbers, options).
8) 3 action owners and dates (who will do what next).

QBR AGENDA (15–30 minute exec sponsor version)
- 0:00–0:03: Opening & one-liner health summary (CSM)
- 0:03–0:08: Business impact highlights (customer-led wins, revenue enablement)
- 0:08–0:14: Operational health (traffic, latency, errors, cost)
- 0:14–0:20: Risks & mitigations (incidents, capacity, compliance)
- 0:20–0:25: Roadmap & product opportunities (how Redwood will help next quarter)
- 0:25–0:30: Ask & close (renewal timing or commitment changes, approve pilot)

DATA SNAPSHOT FIELDS (one-slide or email summary)
- MAU/requests by route (last 90 days)
- Avg tokens per request and total tokens consumed
- Percent of requests served from cache/prefix hits (if instrumented)
- SLOs: P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, throttled requests
- Unit cost: effective $ per 1k tokens vs last quarter
- Feature usage (function calls, tool calling, streaming vs non-streaming)

RISK SIGNALS (early-warning indicators)
- Sudden drop in requests but steady revenue (possible integration break)
- Burst in error rate > 3x baseline for > 1 hour
- Sustained cost-per-token growth > 20% quarter over quarter without product change
- Repeated feature requests not supported by current model (signals unmet product need)
- Extension of shadow environment beyond planned pilot window

RISK SCORE (recommended template)
- Green: No outstanding incidents; on-commit usage stable; renewal on-track
- Amber: One or two moderate risks; small technical debt; need product/SE support
- Red: Material risk to renewal (production regression, unmet SLA, executive churn)

RENEWAL PLAYBOOK (high-level steps)
1) T-90 days: Run consumption vs commit; raise early pricing options if overrun likely. Owner: Renewal Rep + CSM.
2) T-60 days: Sponsor strategic check (this playbook), present capacity options and ROI.
3) T-30 days: Formal renewal proposal + executive email recapping impact and recommended option.
4) T-14 days: Follow-up and close or escalate to AE/leader for concessions.

MEETING PREP CHECKLIST (to-do before sponsor call)
- Generate 1-slide health snapshot and 1-slide roadmap alignment (use template).
- Pull incident timeline for the quarter and short remediation steps.
- Verify billing/commit numbers with Finance (sheet ref)
- Coordinate with SE to prep any demo or technical appendix.
- Draft sponsor email (short) to send after meeting with decisions/action items.

TEMPLATES BELOW (copy + personalize)
1) Short sponsor update (DECK SLIDE or TALKING POINTS)
One-liner: "Overall health: Green. {{customer_name}} continues to scale usage on model X; latency P95 improved 12% after runtime tuning. Renewal on-track for {{renewal_month}}.
Top wins: (1) Reduced per-token spend by 18% via batching and quantized model; (2) Launch of new assistant flow increased conversion 6pp.
Primary risk: Spotty throughput on region eu-west-1 during burst windows — SE has a mitigation: temporary routing to dedicated pool + infra autoscale rule.
Ask: Approve 10% increase in committed capacity for Q3 to avoid throttled requests.
"

2) Customer-facing quarterly recap email (detailed)
Subject: Redwood Q{quarter} recap for {{customer_name}} — performance, risks, and next steps
Hi {{sponsor_first_name}},

Quick recap of Q{quarter} for {{customer_name}} — focusing on impact, stability, and recommended next steps.

Highlights:
- Usage: {{total_tokens}} tokens consumed (+24% QoQ) with peak request window at {timestamp}
- Business impact: Assistant flow A increased conversion from X to Y (estimated revenue uplift $Z)
- Performance: P95 latency improved to {p95}ms; error rate steady at {err}%
- Cost: Effective $/1k tokens is ${cost_token} after optimizations

Risks & actions:
- eu-west-1 burst throughput — mitigation: temporary routing to dedicated pool; ETA to full fix: 2 weeks (owner: SE Samir Rao)
- Model hallucination for finance domain — mitigation: added prompt guardrails + new eval set; monitoring in place

Proposed asks:
- Approve a 10% increase in committed capacity to cover projected Q{q+1} usage (benefit: lower unit price and guaranteed throughput)
- Schedule a 45-min technical sync between {{customer_infra_owner}} and Redwood infra to finalize routing policy

Next steps:
- I will follow up with an updated renewal worksheet and a one-page ROI document by {date}.
- If this week works, propose Wed 10:00–10:45 for the renewal discussion.

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
CSM, Redwood Inference

VARIANT: Short executive email (one-paragraph)
Subject: {{customer_name}} Q{quarter} snapshot — ask: capacity increase
Hi {{sponsor_first_name}},
Topline: Health is Green. Usage up 24% QoQ, P95 latency improved, but we see forecasted commit overrun in 6 weeks. Ask: approve 10% capacity bump so we keep latency and unit cost stable. I can send the renewal worksheet and ROI in a follow-up.

NOTES TO SELF / DRAFT IDEAS
- Consider offering staged commit increase: 5% now + 5% near mid-quarter based on metrics (reduces friction).
- Add a short ROI appendix that translates token usage into product KPIs (conversions, chat resolution time).
- For enterprise customers, include a compliance & audit appendix for Private deployments.

CUSTOMIZATION GUIDANCE
- For Dedicated accounts, emphasize throughput guarantees and burst policy options.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) accounts, emphasize upgrade windows and change freeze schedules.
- For startup PLG customers, emphasize cost-per-token optimization and self-serve tips.

FOLLOW UP CADENCE AFTER QBR
- Day 1: Send recap email with attached one-pager + renewal worksheet.
- Day 7: If no reply, quick check-in note and attach a 1-slide visual of forecast.
- Day 21: Escalate to AE with proposed commercial options.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED
- Should we standardize an "early renewal discount" threshold (e.g., commit increase >25%)? (ask REVOPS)
- How to instrument cache/prefix hit telemetry for all new Dedicated customers? (ask eng/infra)

APPENDIX / LINKS
- Renewal worksheet template: CONFLUENCE-RENEWAL-WKSHT
- QBR slide template: github.com/redwood-inference/qs-templates
- Incident timeline query: JIRA-CSI-78

END OF DRAFT

-- quick checklist before publishing: replace placeholders, attach ROI, confirm commit numbers with Finance, and ping SE to confirm mitigation ETA.
